days.title: Stops you must make (school buses, trains, emergency vehicles, stop lines)
Night, weather, and emergencies (skids, flooding, breakdowns)
Phones, seat belts, crashes, and sharing the road

qs.q: What does an eight-sided (octagon) sign mean?
qs.a: Stop
o: Yield
Railroad ahead
No passing
qs.why: The octagon is the only eight-sided sign. It is always red, and it means you must come to a complete stop.

qs.q: What does a triangular (three-sided) sign pointing down mean?
qs.a: Slow down and yield to traffic
o: Always come to a complete stop
Signal and go at regular speed
Railroad crossing ahead
qs.why: A yield sign means slow down and yield to traffic. If no cars are coming, you do not have to come to a complete stop. If traffic is heavy, always stop.

qs.q: What does an orange sign color mean?
qs.a: Construction and maintenance warning
o: General warning of hazards on the road ahead
School zones
Motorist services
qs.why: Orange is used only for construction and maintenance signs.

qs.q: What does a yellow sign color mean?
qs.a: General warning
o: Construction and maintenance warning
Guidance and directions
Public recreation areas
qs.why: Yellow is the background for warning signs (except where orange is used) and school signs.

qs.q: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
qs.a: A hazardous or unexpected condition ahead
o: A special law or regulation that you must obey
A railroad crossing is here
A stop sign is required
qs.why: Diamond signs call for caution and usually a slower speed.

qs.q: What does a round (circular) sign mean?
qs.a: A railroad crossing is ahead
o: A school zone with children is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
A hospital is ahead
qs.why: The round sign always means you are approaching a railroad grade crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

qs.q: What does a blue sign color mean?
qs.a: Motorist services and information
o: Guidance and directions on interstate highways
Public recreation areas
Construction warning
qs.why: Blue is for motorist services, including police services and rest areas.

qs.q: What does a green sign color mean?
qs.a: Guidance (directions)
o: Motorist services
Public recreation areas
General warning
qs.why: Green is used for guide signs and mileposts.

qs.q: What shape are regulatory signs (like speed limits and lane use)?
qs.a: Rectangle
o: Diamond
Circle
Triangle
qs.why: A regulatory sign is always a rectangle, telling you about laws and regulations.

qs.q: What does a fluorescent yellow-green sign color mean?
qs.a: School zones and pedestrian areas
o: Construction and maintenance zones
Rest areas
Railroad crossings
qs.why: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school zones and pedestrian areas like crosswalks.

qs.q: What should you do when a steady yellow light appears?
qs.a: Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely
o: Speed up to get through before it turns red
Keep going at the same speed
Slam on the brakes, even if you are already in the intersection
qs.why: Yellow means the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Do not speed up to try to get through before the light turns red.

qs.q: What should you do at a flashing red light?
qs.a: Come to a complete stop, like a stop sign
o: Slow down and go with caution
Stop only if you see cross traffic coming toward you
Treat it as a yield sign
qs.why: Flashing red means a complete stop, the same as a stop sign. Look both ways, yield, and go when safe.

qs.q: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
qs.a: Slow down and go through with caution
o: Come to a complete stop, just like at a stop sign
Speed up to clear the intersection
Stop and wait for a green light
qs.why: Flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.

qs.q: What does a green turn arrow (protected turn) mean?
qs.a: You may turn that way, and you have the right-of-way
o: You must yield to all oncoming traffic before you turn
You may go in any direction
You must stop, then turn
qs.why: When the arrow is green you have the right of way and may go only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

qs.q: Your lane has a red arrow, but other lanes have green and the path looks clear. May you turn?
qs.a: No, all turns are prohibited
o: Yes, if the path through the intersection is clear
Yes, after a complete stop
Yes, if you signal first
qs.why: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have green.

qs.q: What does a yellow left arrow mean?
qs.a: Your protected turn is ending, so get ready to yield
o: You may turn left with the right-of-way
You must stop now and wait for the next green light
Oncoming traffic must stop for you
qs.why: When the arrow changes to yellow, the protected turn is about to end. Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

qs.q: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean?
qs.a: Turn left after yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians
o: You have the right-of-way to turn left, and oncoming cars must stop
You may not turn left at all
You must stop before turning left
qs.why: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Wait for a safe gap.

qs.q: What color lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
qs.a: Yellow
o: White
Blue
Orange
qs.why: Lines separating traffic moving in opposite directions are yellow.

qs.q: What color lines separate lanes of traffic going the same direction?
qs.a: White
o: Yellow
Blue
Orange
qs.why: Multiple lanes of traffic flowing in the same direction are separated by white lane markings.

qs.q: The center has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is on your side. What does this mean?
qs.a: You may pass when it is safe
o: You are not allowed to pass here, even if no traffic is coming
You may only make right turns here
You must drive below the speed limit
qs.why: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the passing zone and may pass when it is safe. If the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.

qs.q: When must you yield to pedestrians at a crosswalk?
qs.a: When they are in or about to enter the crosswalk
o: Only when they are in the middle of the street
Only at crosswalks that have a WALK signal showing
Only at marked crosswalks
qs.why: You must yield to pedestrians who are in or about to enter the crosswalk or street. Not all crosswalks are marked.

qs.q: A pedestrian is using a white cane with a red tip or a guide dog. What must you do?
qs.a: Always yield to the pedestrian
o: Honk so the pedestrian knows where you are
Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk
Drive around the pedestrian slowly
qs.why: Always yield to blind pedestrians carrying a white or red-tipped white cane or using a guide dog.

qs.q: You are entering a main road from a driveway or parking lot. Who must yield?
qs.a: You must yield to all vehicles on the main road
o: Vehicles already on the main road must yield to you
Whoever is going faster goes first
Whoever honks first goes first
qs.why: When entering a main road from a driveway, alley, parking lot or roadside, yield to all vehicles already on it.

qs.q: Your light turns green. What must you still do?
qs.a: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection
o: Go immediately, because a green light gives you the right of way
Honk to clear the intersection
Wait three seconds before moving
qs.why: Green means go IF the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.

qs.q: At an ALL-WAY stop, who goes first?
qs.a: The vehicle that got there first
o: The biggest vehicle at the intersection
The vehicle that is going straight
The vehicle on the left side
qs.why: At all-way stops, all vehicles stop, and the first to arrive goes first.

qs.q: Two vehicles reach an all-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?
qs.a: The vehicle on the right
o: The vehicle on the left
The faster vehicle
The vehicle turning left
qs.why: If more than one vehicle arrives at the same time, yield to the vehicle on the right.

qs.q: You have a green light (not an arrow) and want to turn left. Who must you yield to?
qs.a: Oncoming vehicles
o: No one, because green gives you the right-of-way
Only vehicles behind you
Only vehicles turning right
qs.why: The green signal gives permission to go, but you must yield to oncoming vehicles if turning left.

qs.q: At a “T” intersection, your road ends at a main road. Who must yield?
qs.a: You must yield to traffic from both directions
o: Main road traffic must yield to you
Only traffic coming from your left yields
Whoever reaches the intersection first goes
qs.why: Vehicles on the road that ends must yield to traffic from both directions on the main road.

qs.q: A traffic signal is not working at all. What does Tennessee law require?
qs.a: Treat it as an all-way stop
o: Treat it as a yield for everyone
Go through if you are on the bigger road
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
qs.why: If a signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop.

qs.q: May you enter an intersection if you cannot get all the way through it without stopping?
qs.a: No, wait until traffic ahead clears
o: Yes, if your light is green
Yes, if you are turning
Yes, if traffic is moving slowly
qs.why: Do not enter unless you can get through without stopping. Blocking an intersection can get you a ticket.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways?
qs.a: 70 mph
o: 65 mph
75 mph
80 mph
qs.why: The interstate maximum is 70 mph. Drive that fast only in ideal conditions. Some sections have a lower posted limit.

qs.q: Under normal conditions, what is the closest you should follow another vehicle?
qs.a: No closer than two seconds
o: No closer than one second
No closer than one car length
No closer than five seconds
qs.why: If you reach the fixed point before counting to two seconds, slow down. Repeat until you are at least two seconds behind.

qs.q: In bad weather, at night, at higher interstate speeds, or when following a motorcycle, what following distance should you use?
qs.a: At least four seconds
o: At least one second
At least two seconds
At least three car lengths
qs.why: Increase from two seconds to a minimum of four seconds for better reaction time in these conditions.

qs.q: What does the Basic Speed Rule teach?
qs.a: Drive at a speed that is safe for the conditions
o: Always drive at exactly the posted speed limit
Drive 5 mph under the posted limit
Drive as fast as the car ahead of you
qs.why: The Basic Speed Rule is a safety principle, not a law. It does not set an exact limit. The conditions decide what speed is safe.

qs.q: Unless another speed is posted, what is the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways?
qs.a: 55 mph
o: 45 mph
60 mph
65 mph
qs.why: Unless posted otherwise, the limit on these highways is 55 mph.

qs.q: At what speeds does the two-second rule for following at a safe distance hold true?
qs.a: At any speed
o: Only at speeds up to 30 mph
Only at speeds up to 55 mph
Only at speeds up to 45 mph
qs.why: The two-second rule works at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits. In bad weather, at night, and at higher interstate speeds, increase it to at least four seconds.

qs.q: To check your following distance, you watch the car ahead pass a fixed point, like a sign post. What do you do next?
qs.a: Count seconds until you reach that spot
o: Count the cars between you and it
Measure the distance in car lengths instead
Check your speedometer and mirrors
qs.why: Count “one-thousand and one, one-thousand and two” until you reach the same point.

qs.q: Most rear-end crashes are caused by drivers who are doing what?
qs.a: Tailgating (following too closely)
o: Driving under the speed limit
Using their turn signals
Driving with headlights on
qs.why: Rear-end crashes are common, and most are caused by tailgating drivers.

qs.q: When are school zone speed limits in effect?
qs.a: When children are going to or from school, or at recess
o: Only from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on weekdays, all year
Only when a police officer is parked in the zone
All day and night, every day of the whole year
qs.why: School zone speed limits are in effect when children are going to or from school, or during a school recess.

qs.q: With anti-lock brakes (ABS), how should you press the brake pedal to stop?
qs.a: Press down firmly and hold it without pumping
o: Pump it quickly several times
Light taps every second
Press it, then release, then press again
qs.why: With ABS, keep firm, steady pressure. Pumping the pedal disengages the anti-lock system.

qs.q: At a stop sign with a clearly marked stop line, where must you stop?
qs.a: Behind the stop line
o: With your front wheels on the line
Past the line where you can see
At the edge of the cross street
qs.why: If there is a white stop line, you must stop your vehicle behind it.

qs.q: An emergency vehicle with a siren is approaching. What does Tennessee law require you to do?
qs.a: Pull to the right edge and stop
o: Speed up to get out of the way
Stop right where you are in the lane
Pull to the left edge and keep going
qs.why: Yield, drive as close as possible to the right edge or curb, and stop until it passes or a police officer directs you.

qs.q: A school bus has yellow lights flashing. What does this mean?
qs.a: The bus is about to stop, so slow down and get ready to stop
o: The bus is moving, so it is safe to pass it now
Children are getting on or off the bus right now
The bus has broken down and needs your help
qs.why: Yellow flashing lights mean the bus is about to stop to load or unload children.

qs.q: A school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm out. When may you start driving again?
qs.a: When the red lights stop, the stop arm goes in, and the bus starts moving
o: As soon as the children have reached the sidewalk safely
After you have waited 30 seconds and see no more children
When the bus driver honks the horn twice to signal you
qs.why: Wait until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving.

qs.q: A school bus is stopped at an intersection loading children. Which drivers must stop?
qs.a: Drivers from all directions
o: Only drivers behind the bus
Only drivers facing the bus
Only drivers turning right
qs.why: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load or unload, drivers from ALL directions must stop.

qs.q: At a crossing with lights and a gate, when may you go after a train passes?
qs.a: When the gates are up and the lights stop flashing
o: As soon as the train passes your car
When the gates start to rise
When the lights stop flashing, even if the gates are still down
qs.why: Stop when the lights begin flashing, before the gate comes down. Remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop.

qs.q: A train is coming. How far from the railroad tracks must you stop?
qs.a: Between 15 and 50 feet
o: Between 5 and 10 feet
Between 50 and 100 feet
At least 100 feet
qs.why: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the tracks. Never stop on the tracks.

qs.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches. What should you do?
qs.a: Drive on through, then pull over
o: Stop right there in the intersection
Back up out of the intersection
Turn left right away to get clear
qs.why: Drive on through the intersection before pulling over, or you may block the emergency vehicle's path.

qs.q: You are on a highway divided by a median that cars cannot drive on. A school bus is stopped on the other side with its red lights flashing. What should you do?
qs.a: You don't have to stop, but drive carefully
o: Stop until the bus starts moving again
Stop for 10 seconds, then go slowly
Speed up so you pass the bus quickly
qs.why: On a highway divided by a median or barrier that cars cannot drive on, drivers on the other side do not have to stop, but they must drive with caution.

qs.q: You are stopped at a red light when an emergency vehicle approaches. The light turns green before it passes. What should you do?
qs.a: Stay stopped until it passes
o: Go ahead, because the light is green
Turn right as soon as it turns green
Pull forward into the intersection
qs.why: If the light is red, stay where you are. Do NOT go on green until the emergency vehicle has passed.

qs.q: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?
qs.a: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
o: 11 o'clock and 6 o'clock
7 o'clock and 5 o'clock
10 o'clock and 12 o'clock
qs.why: Put your left hand at 9 o'clock and your right hand at 3 o'clock. This position helps avoid injury if the air bag opens.

qs.q: How far before a turn must you turn on your turn signal?
qs.a: At least 50 feet
o: At least 10 feet
At least 25 feet
At least 500 feet
qs.why: Turn on your signal at least 50 feet before the turn or lane change.

qs.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, may you turn right on a red light?
qs.a: Yes, after a complete stop, if there are no pedestrians or cross traffic
o: No, never on a red light
Yes, without stopping if the road is clear
Yes, but only between midnight and 6 a.m. when traffic is light
qs.why: Unless posted otherwise, you may turn right on red after a complete stop when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

qs.q: Does using your turn signal give you the right-of-way?
qs.a: No, signaling does not give you the right-of-way
o: Yes, as soon as you turn your signal on
Yes, once you have signaled for 50 feet
Yes, but only when you are driving on two-lane roads
qs.why: Signals tell others your plan, but they do NOT give you the right-of-way.

qs.q: When making a right turn, which lane should you turn into?
qs.a: The lane closest to the right curb
o: The lane closest to the center line
Any open lane on the new street
The lane farthest to the left
qs.why: Get close to the right curb before turning, and turn into the travel lane closest to the right curb.

qs.q: Who has the right-of-way when you reach a roundabout?
qs.a: Vehicles already in the roundabout
o: Vehicles that are entering the roundabout
The largest vehicle, such as a truck
Whichever driver honks the horn first
qs.why: Yield to vehicles already circulating. Enter when there is a gap.

qs.q: About how far back from the steering wheel should your body be?
qs.a: 10 to 12 inches
o: 6 to 8 inches
18 to 24 inches
3 to 5 inches
qs.why: Sit about 10 to 12 inches back. At this distance an air bag hits your chest, not your chin or face.

qs.q: A bicyclist holds the left arm out, bent up at the elbow, hand pointing upward. What does this signal mean?
qs.a: Right turn
o: Left turn
Stopping or slowing
Go ahead and pass
qs.why: Left arm bent upward at 90 degrees means right turn. A rider may also point the right arm straight out to the right.

qs.q: Making a left turn from a two-way street onto a two-way street, which lane should you turn into?
qs.a: The lane just to the right of the center line
o: The lane closest to the right curb
Whichever lane has the least traffic
The center turn lane of the new street, if there is one
qs.why: Turn into the first lane past the center line. Never turn wide into the right lane, because oncoming drivers who are turning right will use that lane.

qs.q: Which lane must you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?
qs.a: The lane nearest the left curb
o: The lane nearest the center of the street
The lane nearest the right curb
Any lane, if you signal
qs.why: From a one-way street, approach the turn in the lane nearest the left curb.

qs.q: When you pass a bicycle going the same direction as you, how much space does the law require?
qs.a: 3 feet
o: 1 foot
2 feet
6 feet
qs.why: The law requires at least 3 feet between you and the bicycle, kept until you are safely past.

qs.q: What do broken white lines between lanes mean?
qs.a: You may change lanes or pass if it is safe
o: You may never change lanes
Traffic on the other side is going the opposite way
The lane is ending soon
qs.why: Broken white lines mean you may cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

qs.q: What do two solid yellow lines between lanes mean?
qs.a: No passing from either direction
o: Passing allowed from either direction
Passing allowed only from the left side
Passing allowed when no cars are coming
qs.why: Two solid yellow lines mean you MAY NOT cross from either direction, even if no oncoming traffic is in view.

qs.q: Before changing lanes, how do you check your blind spot?
qs.a: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
o: Check only your inside rearview mirror
Check only your outside side mirror
Honk your horn once and then move over
qs.why: Mirrors alone miss vehicles beside you. Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

qs.q: Should you pass when approaching a hill or curve?
qs.a: No, do not pass
o: Yes, if you go fast
Yes, if you honk
Yes, if the car ahead is slow
qs.why: Do not pass when approaching a hill or curve, because you cannot see oncoming traffic.

qs.q: You have a yellow line on your right and a white line on your left. What does this mean?
qs.a: You are going the wrong way
o: You are in the correct lane
You are in a passing zone
You are in a turn lane
qs.why: If you find yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.

qs.q: May you share a lane with a motorcycle?
qs.a: No, a motorcycle has the right to the full lane
o: Yes, if the motorcycle is riding near the edge
Yes, on roads with a speed limit over 45 mph
Yes, if you are both going the same speed
qs.why: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane. You must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

qs.q: After you pass a vehicle, when is it safest to return to the driving lane?
qs.a: When you see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror
o: As soon as your front bumper is past the other car's front bumper
When the other driver waves you over with a hand signal
As soon as you are side by side with the other vehicle
qs.why: Do not count on other drivers to make room. Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.

qs.q: On a two-lane road, when may you pass another vehicle on the right?
qs.a: When it is turning left, if it is safe
o: Whenever it is going below the limit
By driving on the paved shoulder
By using an empty bike lane
qs.why: On a two-lane road, you may pass on the right only when the other vehicle is turning left and it is safe. Never drive on the shoulder to pass.

qs.q: Where are a truck's blind spots, or No-Zones?
qs.a: Right in front, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind
o: Only directly behind the truck, up to 20 feet
Only on the left side of the cab, near the driver's door
Only in front of the truck, up to 500 feet
qs.why: A truck's blind spots are immediately in front, on either side, and up to 200 feet in the rear.

qs.q: When pulling out of any parking space, including a parallel space, what must you do?
qs.a: Look, signal, and yield
o: Honk and pull out
Pull out fast to merge
Wait for a car to wave you in
qs.why: A driver must look, signal and yield the right-of-way when coming out of any parking space.

qs.q: Which of these is an illegal place to park?
qs.a: On a bridge or in a tunnel
o: In a marked parking space
20 feet past a fire hydrant
In a parking lot
qs.why: It is illegal to park on any bridge or in a tunnel.

qs.q: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
qs.a: 15 feet
o: 5 feet
10 feet
30 feet
qs.why: You may NOT park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

qs.q: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
qs.a: 20 feet
o: 5 feet
10 feet
50 feet
qs.why: You may NOT park in a crosswalk or within 20 feet of one.

qs.q: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a traffic signal or stop sign?
qs.a: 30 feet
o: 10 feet
15 feet
50 feet
qs.why: No parking within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or other traffic control device.

qs.q: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
qs.a: 50 feet
o: 15 feet
20 feet
100 feet
qs.why: You may NOT park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

qs.q: After parallel parking, your car should be no farther than how far from the curb?
qs.a: 18 inches
o: 6 inches
12 inches
24 inches
qs.why: When you finish parallel parking, you should be no more than 18 inches from the curb.

qs.q: You park facing DOWNHILL next to a curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
qs.a: Toward the curb
o: Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Toward the center of the road
qs.why: Turn the wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. If the car rolls, it rolls into the curb.

qs.q: You park facing UPHILL next to a curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
qs.a: Away from the curb
o: Toward the curb
Straight ahead
Toward the edge of the road
qs.why: Turn wheels away from the curb. If the car rolls back, it rolls into the curb and stops.

qs.q: You park on a hill with NO curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
qs.a: Toward the edge of the road
o: Toward the center of the road
Straight ahead
Away from the edge of the road
qs.why: With no curb, uphill or downhill, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (right) so the car rolls away from traffic.

qs.q: You miss your exit on the interstate. What must you do?
qs.a: Go on to the next exit
o: Back up on the shoulder to the exit
Make a U-turn at the median
Stop on the shoulder and wait
qs.why: It is illegal to back up, make a U-turn, or cross the median on the interstate.

qs.q: You are driving slower than the flow of traffic on the interstate. Which lane must you use?
qs.a: The right lane
o: The left lane
The center lane
The shoulder
qs.why: Slower traffic must stay in the right lane.

qs.q: When you enter an interstate highway, what should you do?
qs.a: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear
o: Stop at the end of the ramp, check for cars, then enter when it is safe
Slow down to 25 mph before you enter the traffic lane
Drive onto the shoulder first, then merge when clear
qs.why: Use the ramp to speed up to the speed of interstate traffic. Then merge when the way is clear.

qs.q: You are merging onto the interstate from a ramp. Who must yield the right-of-way?
qs.a: You, the driver entering from the ramp
o: The cars already on the interstate
Whichever car is going slower
Whichever car is larger
qs.why: Drivers on the interstate should make room if they can, but the entering driver must yield.

qs.q: When you leave the interstate, when should you start to slow down?
qs.a: After you enter the deceleration lane
o: While you are still in the travel lane
Before you change lanes toward the exit
Only when you reach the end of the ramp
qs.why: Keep your speed until you are in the deceleration (exit) lane, then slow to the ramp's posted speed.

qs.q: On a multi-lane road, you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing on the roadside. What does the Move Over Law require?
qs.a: Move over a lane away from it, or slow down if you can't
o: Stop completely behind it until it drives away
Honk your horn and keep going at the same speed
Turn on your high beams and pass it quickly
qs.why: Change to a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle. If you can't do that safely, slow down and drive with caution.

qs.q: When should you merge for a lane closure ahead in a work zone?
qs.a: As soon as possible, when you first see the work zone
o: At the very last moment before the lane ends
Only after you can see the workers on the road
Only when a flagger tells you to
qs.why: Merge as soon as possible. If you wait until the last moment to merge, you can get a ticket and you can cause a crash.

qs.q: Who is allowed to cross an interstate median (use an emergency crossover)?
qs.a: Only emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews
o: Any driver who missed their exit and needs to turn around
Any driver when no other cars are around
Trucks and buses that need to turn around
qs.why: Regular drivers may never cross the median. If you miss your exit, go on to the next exit.

qs.q: Your car has trouble on the interstate. What should you do first?
qs.a: Move to the right shoulder and turn on your emergency flashers
o: Stop right where you are in your lane and turn on your flashers
Move to the left shoulder and turn off your lights
Keep driving slowly in the right lane
qs.why: Get off the road to the right shoulder or emergency stopping area as soon as you can, and warn other traffic.

qs.q: Safe interstate driving demands complete awareness of higher speed driving and what else?
qs.a: Constant alertness by the driver
o: A vehicle with a large engine
Driving in the left lane at all times
Keeping up with the fastest car
qs.why: Interstate driving needs both complete awareness of higher speed driving and constant alertness.

qs.q: You come to a road covered by flood water. What should you do?
qs.a: Turn around and find another way
o: Drive through slowly in low gear
Drive through quickly to keep momentum
Follow another car through the water
qs.why: Do not drive into flood water. The water may be deeper than it looks, and the road under it may be washed out.

qs.q: Your vehicle stalls on the railroad tracks. What should you do first?
qs.a: Get everyone out right away and away from the tracks
o: Keep trying to restart the car until the engine starts
Stay in the car with your safety belt on
Push the car off the tracks yourself
qs.why: All occupants should exit immediately and get away from the tracks, even if you do not see a train.

qs.q: How does driving at night compare to driving in the daytime?
qs.a: More dangerous, because your headlights limit how far you can see
o: Safer, because there is less traffic and there are fewer distractions
Safer, so you can increase your speed
Just as safe, as long as your lights are on
qs.why: Your range of visibility at night is limited by your headlights, so drive slower.

qs.q: At night, when must your headlights be on?
qs.a: From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
o: From sunset until sunrise
From 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise
From 15 minutes after sunset until 15 minutes before sunrise
qs.why: Tennessee law requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

qs.q: At night, you must dim your high beams when meeting or overtaking a vehicle within how many feet?
qs.a: 500 feet
o: 200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
qs.why: Dim your lights when meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet.

qs.q: Why should you use low beams, not high beams, in fog?
qs.a: Low beams let you see better and help others see you
o: Low beams make your car harder for others to see
High beams drain the car battery in fog
High beams make the fog get thicker
qs.why: In fog or mist, high beam light reflects back into your eyes. Low beams put the light on the road.

qs.q: How can you tell if carbon monoxide is in your car?
qs.a: You can't tell, because it has no taste, smell, or color
o: It has a strong smell like rotten eggs or gasoline
It looks like a light gray smoke
It tastes bitter in your mouth
qs.why: Carbon monoxide from an engine can kill. It has no taste, no smell, and cannot be seen.

qs.q: Your car starts to hydroplane on a wet road. What should you do?
qs.a: Slow down gradually by letting up on the gas
o: Slam on the brakes right away
Speed up a little so you can push through the water
Turn the wheel sharply to the side
qs.why: When hydroplaning, your tires lose the grip needed to steer and brake. Don't slam on the brakes.

qs.q: Your car does NOT have anti-lock brakes and starts to skid. What is the general rule?
qs.a: Ease off the brake and steer in the direction of the skid
o: Press the brake pedal harder and steer away from the skid
Pump the brake and hold the wheel straight
Speed up and steer opposite the skid
qs.why: Without ABS, ease off the brake and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid, if you can do so safely.

qs.q: What does continuous hard braking on ice and snow often do?
qs.a: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control
o: Helps you stop faster on the ice
Keeps the brakes warm so they do not freeze up in the cold
Makes the tires grip the road better
qs.why: Keep a safe speed for icy conditions so you don't need hard braking.

qs.q: What is the only thing that can sober up a person who has been drinking?
qs.a: Time
o: Drinking coffee
Taking a cold shower
Exercising
qs.why: Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not speed up how fast the liver removes alcohol.

qs.q: What is the lowest BAC that is always illegal for drivers 21 and older in Tennessee?
qs.a: 0.08 percent
o: 0.10 percent
0.15 percent
0.20 percent
qs.why: Lower limits apply to drivers under 21. You can still get a DUI below 0.08 if you are impaired.

qs.q: As the percentage of alcohol in your blood (BAC) goes up, what do you become?
qs.a: More intoxicated
o: More sober
More coordinated
More alert
qs.why: The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.

qs.q: What penalty does driving under the influence of drugs carry?
qs.a: The same penalty as for alcohol
o: A lesser penalty than for alcohol
No penalty at all
A penalty only if the drug is illegal
qs.why: The penalties are the same for alcohol and drugs, even prescription or over-the-counter drugs.

qs.q: What is the lowest BAC at which a driver age 16 to 20 can be convicted of underage driving while impaired?
qs.a: 0.02 percent
o: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.10 percent
qs.why: Being under the influence of alcohol or any other intoxicant also counts.

qs.q: How does the alcohol in a 12-ounce beer compare to a 1-ounce shot of whiskey?
qs.a: It is about the same
o: The beer has much less
The beer has much more
The beer has none
qs.why: A 12-ounce beer has about as much alcohol as a 1-ounce shot of whiskey. Drinking beer instead of whiskey does not make you any safer.

qs.q: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?
qs.a: Alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination
o: Only reaction time
Only alertness and concentration, but not reaction time or coordination
None of them, if you feel fine
qs.why: Alcohol also affects judgment and vision, the two most important driving abilities.

qs.q: What does Tennessee's Implied Consent law mean?
qs.a: By driving, you agree to be tested for alcohol or drugs if an officer asks
o: Traffic laws apply even without any signs, markings, or signals at an intersection
The owner of a vehicle will carry proper insurance
You agree to let police search your car any time
qs.why: The officer must have reasonable grounds to believe you are driving under the influence.

qs.q: You had three beers in the past hour. About how long will it take for the alcohol to leave your blood?
qs.a: About three hours
o: About one hour
About two hours
About thirty minutes
qs.why: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink.

qs.q: Which of these can get a driver license revoked or suspended?
qs.a: Fraudulently altering a driver license
o: Renewing your license a week early
Driving a borrowed car with permission
Moving to another county in Tennessee
qs.why: Frequent violations that add up to 12 or more points in 12 months can also lead to suspension for adults.

qs.q: Under Tennessee's Hands Free law, which is illegal for a driver?
qs.a: Holding a phone with any part of your body
o: Listening to the radio while driving
Talking on the phone in hands-free mode
Using the car's built-in rear camera
qs.why: It is illegal to hold a phone with any part of your body, to text, to watch video, or to record or broadcast video while driving.

qs.q: Who must wear a safety belt any time the vehicle is moving?
qs.a: The driver and all front-seat passengers
o: Only the driver
Only the driver and passengers who are under 18
Only passengers in the back seat
qs.why: Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all front-seat passengers any time the vehicle is in motion.

qs.q: What is the safest place for children 12 and under to ride in a car with air bags?
qs.a: The back seat
o: The front seat
The bed of a pickup truck
The front seat with the seat moved forward
qs.why: Children ages 12 and under are safer in the back seat. Air bags pose a severe risk to children of that age.

qs.q: What are properly adjusted seat head restraints designed to do?
qs.a: Prevent whiplash if you are hit from behind
o: Keep your head straight when you check mirrors
Hold your head still during a sharp turn
Protect your head if the air bag opens
qs.why: Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if you are hit from behind. Adjust them level with the back of your head.

qs.q: How high should you adjust the seat head restraint?
qs.a: Level with the back of your head
o: Level with the base of your neck
Level with the top of your shoulders
Just above the top of your head
qs.why: Adjust the head restraint to a level even with the back of the head.

qs.q: You are involved in a crash. What does the law require first?
qs.a: Stop right away at or near the scene, without blocking traffic
o: Drive to the nearest police station and report the crash in person
Keep driving if no one looks hurt
Stop only if the crash was your fault
qs.why: Turn off the ignition of a damaged car to prevent a fire. Never leave the scene.

qs.q: You are not the first at a crash scene and your help is not needed. What should you do?
qs.a: Slowly drive on and do not get in the way
o: Stop and look to satisfy your curiosity
Slow down to calm your nerves
Park nearby to watch the rescue
qs.why: Slowing down to look at a crash (“accident gazing”) can cause more crashes and block emergency crews.

qs.q: Which statement about car seats is correct?
qs.a: Rear-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Forward-facing if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
o: Forward-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Rear-facing if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
Rear-facing if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Booster seat if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
Booster seat if under 1 year old and under 20 pounds. Seat belt only if 1 through 3 years old and over 20 pounds
qs.why: A child under 1 year old, or any child under 20 pounds, must ride rear-facing. Children 1 through 3 years old who weigh more than 20 pounds must ride forward-facing.

qs.q: How should a pregnant woman wear her safety belt?
qs.a: Lap belt below the abdomen, shoulder belt above the belly
o: Lap belt across the middle of the belly, shoulder belt under the arm
Only the lap belt, without the shoulder belt
Only the shoulder belt, without the lap belt
qs.why: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

qs.q: After a reportable crash, how long does the driver have to file a crash report with the Department of Safety?
qs.a: 20 days
o: 10 days
48 hours
30 days
qs.why: This is required no matter who is to blame.

At an all-way stop

wordings.q: Your mirrors are adjusted correctly. What must you still do before you turn or change lanes?
wordings.a: Turn your head and check your blind spots
o: Look only in the inside mirror
Look only in the side mirrors
Tap the horn to warn any drivers who are beside you
wordings.why: Even properly adjusted mirrors cannot remove all blind spots. Always turn your head and check.

wordings.q: When stopping at a curb to park, how close should you get?
wordings.a: Within 18 inches of the curb
o: Within 36 inches of the curb
Within 6 feet of the curb
Within 30 inches of the curb
wordings.why: Move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

wordings.q: How far should your chest be from the air bag module, according to NHTSA?
wordings.a: 10 to 12 inches
o: 4 to 6 inches
15 to 18 inches
20 to 24 inches
wordings.why: Sit as far as possible from the steering wheel. NHTSA recommends 10 to 12 inches between the chest and the air bag.

wordings.q: A blue sign points to a rest area. What kind of sign is it?
wordings.a: A motorist services sign
o: A warning sign
A regulatory sign
A recreation and cultural interest sign
wordings.why: Blue is the background for motorist services, including police services and rest areas.

wordings.q: You see a flashing arrow panel showing a lane is closed. When should you merge?
wordings.a: Well before you reach the sign
o: Right when you reach the sign
After you pass the sign
Only when cones block your lane
wordings.why: Flashing arrow panels warn you that a lane is closed. Begin to merge into the open lane well before you reach it.

wordings.q: Two vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?
wordings.a: The driver on the right
o: The driver on the left
The larger vehicle
The driver going straight
wordings.why: If two or more vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

wordings.q: You see a sign with a yellow background. What kind of sign is it?
wordings.a: A general warning sign
o: A construction and maintenance sign
A guide sign that gives directions
A motorist services sign
wordings.why: Yellow is the background color for warning signs, except construction and maintenance signs, which are orange. It is also used for school signs.

wordings.q: You see an orange sign ahead. What does the orange color tell you?
wordings.a: Construction and maintenance warning
o: A school zone with children crossing is ahead
Motorist services are nearby
A recreation area is nearby
wordings.why: Orange is used only for construction and maintenance signs.

wordings.q: Signs with a green background give you what kind of information?
wordings.a: Guidance (directions)
o: Construction and maintenance warnings
Motorist services and information
School zone warnings
wordings.why: Green is the background color for guide signs, which give directions, and for mileposts.

wordings.q: You see a fluorescent yellow-green sign. Where are you most likely to be?
wordings.a: In a school zone or pedestrian area
o: In a construction or maintenance work zone
Near a rest area
Near a hospital
wordings.why: Fluorescent yellow-green signs mark school zones and pedestrian areas, such as crosswalks. Watch for children, people on foot, and bicyclists.

wordings.q: A red, eight-sided sign is partly covered by snow, so you cannot read it. What must you do?
wordings.a: Come to a complete stop
o: Slow down and yield
Slow down for a railroad crossing
Keep going if no one is coming
wordings.why: Even when a stop sign is damaged or covered, its eight-sided shape and red color tell you to stop.

wordings.q: You come to an intersection with a sign shaped like a triangle pointing down. What does the sign tell you to do?
wordings.a: Slow down and yield to traffic
o: Always come to a complete stop
Speed up to get ahead of traffic
Stop only if a train is coming
wordings.why: A triangle pointing down is a yield sign. Slow down and yield. If no cars are coming, you do not have to stop completely. If traffic is heavy, always stop.

wordings.q: A round sign is posted beside the road. What does it warn you about?
wordings.a: A railroad crossing is ahead
o: A school crossing is ahead
A sharp curve in the road is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
wordings.why: A round sign always means you are coming to a railroad crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

wordings.q: Signs shaped like a diamond warn you about what?
wordings.a: A hazardous or unexpected condition ahead
o: A law you must obey, like a speed limit
Gas, food, and other services nearby
A place where you must stop
wordings.why: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about a hazard or something unexpected ahead. Be careful and usually slow down.

wordings.q: A speed limit sign is a regulatory sign. What shape is it?
wordings.a: Rectangle
o: Diamond
Circle
Octagon
wordings.why: Regulatory signs, which tell you about laws, speed limits, and lane use, are always rectangles.

wordings.q: Two lanes going your way are divided by a broken white line. May you move into the other lane?
wordings.a: Yes, you may cross it to change lanes or pass if it is safe
o: No, you may never cross a broken white line
Only to make a left turn
Only when a police officer waves you over
wordings.why: Broken white lines between lanes mean you may cross them to change lanes or pass, when it is safe.

wordings.q: The center of the road has two solid yellow lines. A slow truck is ahead, and no cars are coming the other way. May you pass it?
wordings.a: No, you may not cross the lines from either direction
o: Yes, because you can see that no cars are coming the other way
Yes, if you honk first
Yes, if the truck driver waves you on
wordings.why: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction, even when no oncoming traffic is in sight.

wordings.q: You want to pass a slow car. In the center of the road, the broken yellow line is on your side and the solid yellow line is on the other side. What does this mean?
wordings.a: You may pass when it is safe
o: You may never pass on a road with yellow lines
You may pass only on the right shoulder
You must wait for a broken white line
wordings.why: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in a passing zone and may pass when it is safe. When the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.

wordings.q: A traffic light is blinking yellow. What should you do?
wordings.a: Slow down and go through with caution
o: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is clear
Speed up before it turns red
Stop and wait until it turns green
wordings.why: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution.

wordings.q: The traffic light ahead of you changes from green to yellow. What should you do?
wordings.a: Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely
o: Speed up to beat the red light
Keep going at the same speed
Stop right away, even if you are already in the middle of the intersection
wordings.why: Yellow means the light is about to turn red. Stop if you can do so safely. Do not speed up to beat the light.

wordings.q: You are in a left-turn lane, and the signal shows a green arrow pointing left. What does the arrow mean?
wordings.a: You may turn that way, and you have the right-of-way
o: You must yield to all oncoming traffic, then turn
You may go straight or turn
You must stop first, then turn
wordings.why: A green arrow gives you the right-of-way to go in the direction of the arrow. Still yield to cars and people already in the intersection.

wordings.q: You are waiting to turn left on a green arrow. It changes to a steady yellow arrow. What does that mean?
wordings.a: Your protected turn is ending, so get ready to yield
o: You still have the right-of-way, so turn quickly
Oncoming cars must now stop for you
You may turn left only after a full stop
wordings.why: When the arrow turns yellow, your protected turn is ending. Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

wordings.q: The left-turn signal shows a flashing yellow arrow. What may you do?
wordings.a: Turn left after yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians
o: Turn left right away, because oncoming cars must stop
Nothing, because left turns are not allowed
Turn left only after the arrow turns red
wordings.why: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after you yield to all oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait for a safe gap.

wordings.q: Your lane has a red turn arrow. The cars in the lane next to you have a green light. May you make your turn?
wordings.a: No, all turns are prohibited
o: Yes, if no cars are coming
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if the car behind you honks
wordings.why: When the arrow for your lane is red, all turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have green.

wordings.q: The traffic lights at an intersection are completely dark because the power is out. What should you do?
wordings.a: Treat it as an all-way stop
o: Treat it as a yield sign
Go through if you are on the bigger road
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
wordings.why: Tennessee law says a traffic signal that is not working is treated as an all-way stop. Stop as you would at stop signs.

wordings.q: Your high beams are on. You must dim them when an oncoming vehicle is within how many feet?
wordings.a: 500 feet
o: 200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
wordings.why: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet, about one city block.

wordings.q: Your high beams are on and you are following another vehicle. You must dim them when you are within how many feet of it?
wordings.a: 500 feet
o: 100 feet
250 feet
1,000 feet
wordings.why: Dim high beams when following within 500 feet. The glare in the other driver's mirror can blind them.

wordings.q: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
wordings.a: Stop completely, as at a stop sign
o: Slow down and go through with caution
Stop only if other cars are coming
Treat it the same as a green light
wordings.why: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, just like a stop sign.

wordings.q: Is it legal to drive into an intersection and block it after the light changes?
wordings.a: No, it is always illegal, even if there is no sign
o: Yes, if traffic is heavy and moving slowly
No, but only where a sign says so
Yes, as long as you entered before the light changed
wordings.why: It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether or not a "Do Not Block" sign is posted.

wordings.q: Your light turns green, but a vehicle is still in the intersection. What should you do?
wordings.a: Yield to the vehicle in the intersection
o: Go ahead, because you have a green light
Honk your horn to make the vehicle hurry
Go around the vehicle on the right side
wordings.why: Yield to any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green light.

wordings.q: You are turning left on a regular green light (not a green arrow). Who must you yield to?
wordings.a: Oncoming cars going straight or turning right
o: Nobody, because you have a green light
Only pedestrians in the crosswalk
Only oncoming vehicles that are also turning left
wordings.why: When turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, unless you have a protected green arrow.

wordings.q: What color are center lines on two-way streets?
wordings.a: Yellow
o: White
Blue
Red
wordings.why: Center lines on two-way streets are yellow. On one-way streets, they are white.

wordings.q: What color are center lines on one-way streets?
wordings.a: White
o: Yellow
Orange
Blue
wordings.why: One-way street lines are white. Two-way street center lines are yellow.

wordings.q: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lane do you turn into?
wordings.a: The first lane right of the yellow line
o: The lane closest to the right curb
The lane to the left of the yellow line
Any lane, as long as it is clear
wordings.why: Turn sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line. Move to the right lane only after signaling and checking traffic.

wordings.q: You notice the yellow line is on your RIGHT side. What does this mean?
wordings.a: You are on the wrong side, so pull over right away
o: You are in the passing lane of a highway
You are on a one-way street and are going the right way
You are in a turn lane and must turn left
wordings.why: If the yellow line is on your right, you are driving on the wrong side. Pull over immediately.

wordings.q: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?
wordings.a: Go on to the next exit
o: Back up on the shoulder
Stop and wait for a gap
Make a U-turn at a crossover
wordings.why: Do NOT back up. It is illegal to back up on the interstate.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a fire hydrant?
wordings.a: 15 feet away
o: 5 feet away
10 feet away
30 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a crosswalk?
wordings.a: 20 feet away
o: 5 feet away
10 feet away
50 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park in a crosswalk or within 20 feet of one.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a stop sign?
wordings.a: 30 feet away
o: 10 feet away
15 feet away
50 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, a stop sign, or any other traffic control device.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a railroad crossing?
wordings.a: 50 feet away
o: 15 feet away
20 feet away
100 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

wordings.q: You park facing downhill next to a curb. How should you set your front wheels?
wordings.a: Toward the curb
o: Away from the curb
Straight, lined up with the car
Toward the middle of the street
wordings.why: Facing downhill next to a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. If the car rolls, the curb stops it.

wordings.q: You park facing uphill next to a curb. How should you set your front wheels?
wordings.a: Away from the curb
o: Toward the curb
Straight, lined up with the car
Toward the edge of the road
wordings.why: Facing uphill next to a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. If the car rolls back, the back of the front wheel stops against the curb.

wordings.q: You park on a hill beside a road that has no curb. Which way should you point your front wheels?
wordings.a: Toward the edge of the road
o: Toward the middle of the road
Straight, lined up with the car
Away from the edge of the road
wordings.why: With no curb, uphill or downhill, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road, so the car rolls away from traffic if it moves.

wordings.q: You plan to turn right at the next corner. When should your turn signal be on?
wordings.a: At least 50 feet before the turn
o: Only once you start to turn
Only after you stop at the corner
Never, because right turns need no signal
wordings.why: Turn on your turn signal at least 50 feet before you turn.

wordings.q: What is the highest speed Tennessee law allows on an interstate highway?
wordings.a: 70 mph
o: 60 mph
65 mph
75 mph
wordings.why: The highest speed Tennessee law allows on interstate highways is 70 mph. Some stretches have a lower posted limit, and you should go that fast only in good conditions.

wordings.q: You are on a primary state highway, and no speed limit is posted. What is the speed limit?
wordings.a: 55 mph
o: 45 mph
65 mph
70 mph
wordings.why: Unless another speed is posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 mph.

wordings.q: On a state highway with a moderate speed limit, at what speeds does the two-second following rule work?
wordings.a: At any speed
o: Only below 30 mph
Only below 45 mph
Only above 55 mph
wordings.why: The two-second rule holds at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits. In bad weather, at night, and at higher interstate speeds, leave at least four seconds.

wordings.q: What do flashing yellow lights on the front and back of a school bus tell you?
wordings.a: The bus is about to stop, so slow down and get ready to stop
o: The bus is moving, so it is safe to pass it
Children are crossing the road right now
The bus is about to turn left
wordings.why: Flashing yellow lights mean the bus is getting ready to stop to load or unload children. Slow down and be ready to stop.

wordings.q: You have stopped for a school bus that has red flashing lights and its stop arm out. When may you drive on?
wordings.a: When the red lights stop, the stop arm goes in, and the bus starts moving
o: As soon as the last child reaches the sidewalk
When the bus driver honks the horn twice
After you count to 30 and see no children
wordings.why: Wait until the red lights turn off, the stop arm goes back in, and the bus starts moving.

wordings.q: You are at an intersection where a school bus has stopped to let children off. Which drivers must stop?
wordings.a: Drivers from all directions
o: Only drivers behind the bus
Only drivers coming toward the bus
Only drivers who are about to turn
wordings.why: When a school bus stops at an intersection to load or unload children, drivers from all directions must stop until the bus moves again.

wordings.q: A school bus with red lights flashing is stopped on the other side of a divided highway. A median that cars cannot drive on is between you and the bus. What must you do?
wordings.a: You don't have to stop, but drive carefully
o: Stop until the bus starts moving again
Stop, then pass slowly once the stop arm goes in
Honk your horn and keep going at the same speed
wordings.why: On a highway divided by a median or barrier that cars cannot drive on, drivers on the other side do not have to stop, but they should drive with caution.

wordings.q: You turn right onto a street that has two lanes going your way. Which lane should you turn into?
wordings.a: The lane closest to the right curb
o: The lane closest to the center line
Whichever lane has less traffic
The lane farthest to the left
wordings.why: Make a right turn into the travel lane closest to the right curb.

wordings.q: You are on a one-way street and want to turn left. Which lane should you be in before you turn?
wordings.a: The lane nearest the left curb
o: The lane nearest the right curb
The middle lane
Any lane, as long as you signal
wordings.why: To turn left from a one-way street, make your approach in the lane nearest the left curb.

wordings.q: You and two other cars stop at an all-way stop at different times. Which car goes first?
wordings.a: The vehicle that got there first
o: The largest vehicle
The vehicle going straight through the intersection
The vehicle on the left
wordings.why: At an all-way stop, every vehicle stops, and the vehicle that reaches the intersection first goes first.

wordings.q: You hear a siren, and an ambulance is coming up behind you. What must you do?
wordings.a: Pull to the right edge and stop
o: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop where you are in your lane
Pull to the left edge and keep driving
wordings.why: Yield to the ambulance: pull as close as you can to the right edge or curb and stop until it has passed.

wordings.q: You are halfway through an intersection when a fire truck with its siren on comes toward it. What should you do?
wordings.a: Drive on through, then pull over
o: Stop right where you are
Back up out of the intersection
Turn right at once, even if you were going straight
wordings.why: If you are in an intersection, drive on through it before you pull over, so you do not block the emergency vehicle.

wordings.q: You are on a highway with two lanes going your way. A police car is stopped on the right shoulder of your side, with its lights flashing. What must you do?
wordings.a: Move over a lane away from it, or slow down if you can't
o: Stop behind it and wait until it drives away from the shoulder
Keep going at the same speed
Flash your high beams and pass quickly
wordings.why: Move into a lane that is not next to the stopped emergency vehicle, or slow down and drive with caution.

wordings.q: On the interstate in normal conditions, what is the least following distance you should keep behind the vehicle ahead?
wordings.a: 2 seconds
o: 1 second
4 seconds
6 seconds
wordings.why: Stay at least 2 seconds behind. Increase it to at least 4 seconds in bad weather, at night, and on higher speed rural sections.

wordings.q: In bad weather, at night, or on higher-speed rural sections of the interstate, what is the least following distance you should keep?
wordings.a: 4 seconds
o: 2 seconds
3 seconds
6 seconds
wordings.why: The normal minimum is 2 seconds. In these harder conditions, use at least 4 seconds.

wordings.q: How should you use antilock brakes (ABS) in an emergency stop?
wordings.a: Apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal
o: Pump the brake pedal quickly
Tap the pedal lightly over and over
Press, release, and press the pedal again slowly
wordings.why: Push the pedal all the way to the floor if needed, even on wet or icy roads.

wordings.q: For a driver 21 or older, what is the lowest blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at which driving is always illegal in Tennessee?
wordings.a: 0.08 percent
o: 0.02 percent
0.10 percent
0.15 percent
wordings.why: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent is always illegal. You can still be charged with DUI below 0.08 if you are impaired.

wordings.q: What is the lowest blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at which an 18-year-old driver can be convicted of underage driving while impaired?
wordings.a: 0.02 percent
o: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.10 percent
wordings.why: A driver who is at least 16 but not yet 21 can be convicted of underage driving while impaired with a BAC of 0.02 percent or more.

wordings.q: When you cross or enter an intersection, what must you be sure of before you go?
wordings.a: That you can get all the way across without blocking it
o: That the car behind you has stopped completely
That you can make it halfway and wait in the middle lane
That your headlights are on low beam
wordings.why: Do not block intersections. Make sure you have a big enough gap to get all the way across before you enter.

wordings.q: Your car has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and you need to stop quickly. What should you do?
wordings.a: Press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing
o: Pump the brake pedal quickly on and off
Press the brake gently, and let up as soon as the pedal starts to vibrate
Use the parking brake instead of the brake pedal
wordings.why: With ABS, press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing. You may feel the pedal push back. Do NOT let up.

wordings.q: You are braking hard in a car with ABS, and you feel the brake pedal pushing back. What should you do?
wordings.a: Keep the brake pedal pushed down firmly
o: Let up on the brake pedal right away
Pump the brake pedal faster
Shift into neutral and let up on the brake
wordings.why: Pushing back means the ABS is working. Do NOT let up. ABS only works with the pedal pushed down firmly.

wordings.q: Where is it best to place your hands on the steering wheel?
wordings.a: At about the 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions
o: At about the 12 o'clock position with one hand
At about the 6 o'clock position with both hands
At about the 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock positions
wordings.why: Hands at about 9 and 3 o'clock help you turn quickly and keep your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's path.

wordings.q: In a car with ABS, should you pump the brakes in an emergency?
wordings.a: No, never pump the brakes in a car with ABS
o: Yes, pump the brakes quickly to avoid skidding
Yes, pump the brakes if the pedal starts to pulsate
Yes, but only on wet or icy roads
wordings.why: Never pump ABS brakes, even if the pedal pulsates. The ABS is already pumping the brakes for you, much faster.

wordings.q: When you pass a bicyclist going the same direction, how much space does Tennessee law require?
wordings.a: At least 3 feet
o: At least 1 foot
At least 2 feet
At least 10 feet
wordings.why: Pass slowly and leave at least 3 feet between you and the bicycle. Keep that space until you are safely past.

wordings.q: Which lane must slower traffic use?
wordings.a: The right-hand lane
o: The left-hand lane
The center turn lane
Any lane they choose
wordings.why: Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.

wordings.q: The crossing gates are down at a railroad crossing. When may you cross?
wordings.a: Only after the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing
o: As soon as the train passes, even if the gates are still down
Whenever you can safely drive around the gates
When the gates start to go up, even if the lights are still flashing
wordings.why: Never drive around a lowered gate. It is against the law. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

wordings.q: At a railroad crossing with signal devices, where must you stop?
wordings.a: Within 50 feet but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
o: Within 100 feet but no closer than 50 feet from the nearest rail
Within 10 feet but no closer than 5 feet from the nearest rail
Right at the edge of the nearest rail
wordings.why: At crossings with electric or mechanical signals, stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.

wordings.q: You are driving near a large truck. Where are its blind spots, where the driver cannot see you?
wordings.a: Right in front, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind
o: Only directly behind the truck, up to 10 feet
Only next to the driver's door
Only far ahead of the truck, more than 500 feet in front of it
wordings.why: A truck's blind spots, or No-Zones, are right in front of it, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind it.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, a red eight-sided sign, and a yellow diamond. Which sign means you must come to a complete stop? Tap the sign.

then.say: The red eight-sided sign means you must come to a complete stop. No other sign has eight sides, and this sign is always red. The green rectangle gives directions, and the yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead.

wrong.guide-rect: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways. The red eight-sided sign is the one that means you must come to a complete stop, and no other sign has eight sides.
wrong.warning-diamond: The yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead, such as a sharp curve. The red eight-sided sign is the one that means you must come to a complete stop, and no other sign has eight sides.

steps.rule: The octagon is the only eight-sided sign, it is always red, and it means you must come to a complete stop.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a red eight-sided sign, a blue rectangle, and a red and white three-sided sign pointing down. Which sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The red and white three-sided sign pointing down, the yield sign, means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first. When no car is coming you do not have to stop, and when traffic is heavy you always stop. The red eight-sided sign means you must always stop, and the blue rectangle points to services for drivers.

wrong.stop-sign: The red eight-sided sign means you must always come to a complete stop. The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first. When no car is coming, you do not have to stop.
wrong.services-rect: The blue rectangle points to services for drivers, such as a rest area. The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first.

steps.rule: A yield sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first, you need not come to a complete stop when no cars are coming, and you always stop when traffic is heavy.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a yellow circle, a yellow diamond, and a green rectangle. Which sign means a railroad crossing is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead, so you slow down and get ready to stop for a train. A round sign always means a railroad crossing. The yellow diamond warns of other hazards ahead, and the green rectangle gives directions.

wrong.warning-diamond: The yellow diamond warns of a hazard or something unexpected ahead, such as a sharp curve. A round sign always means a railroad crossing, so the yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead.
wrong.guide-rect: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways. A round sign always means a railroad crossing, so the yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead.

steps.rule: A round sign always means you are coming to a railroad crossing, so you slow down and get ready to stop.

steps.prompt: The red eight-sided sign means you stop. The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you let the traffic on the other road go first. The yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead. What tells you what each sign means, even from too far away to read it?
options: Its shape and its color tell you.
The words written on it tell you.
Where it stands beside the road tells you.
steps.answer: Its shape and its color tell you.

then.say: Every sign's shape and color tell you its purpose, so you know what it means before you can read it. Even when snow or dirt covers a stop sign, its eight sides and its red color tell you to stop.

From too far away to read a sign, you cannot read its words, and snow or dirt can cover them. Its shape and its color tell you what it means before you can read it.
wrong.Where it stands beside the road tells yo: The red eight-sided sign, the red and white three-sided sign pointing down and the yellow circle all stand beside the road, and each means something different. Its shape and its color tell you what it means, even before you can read it.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a red eight-sided sign, a green rectangle, a yellow diamond, and a blue rectangle. Which sign means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead, such as a sharp curve? Tap the sign.

then.say: The yellow diamond means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead. A diamond sign calls for care and usually a slower speed. The red eight-sided sign means stop, the green rectangle gives directions, and the blue rectangle points to services for drivers.

wrong.stop-sign: The red eight-sided sign means you must come to a complete stop. The yellow diamond means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead, and it calls for care and usually a slower speed.
wrong.guide-rect: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways. The yellow diamond means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead, and it calls for care and usually a slower speed.
wrong.services-rect: The blue rectangle points to services for drivers, such as a rest area. The yellow diamond means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead, and it calls for care and usually a slower speed.

steps.rule: A diamond sign means a hazardous or unexpected condition is ahead, and it calls for caution and usually a slower speed.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a yellow diamond, a white rectangle, and a yellow circle. Which sign means a law you must obey, such as a speed limit? Tap the sign.

then.say: The white rectangle means a law you must obey, such as a speed limit or which lane to use. A sign that tells you a speed limit or which lane to use is always a rectangle. The yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead, and the yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead.

wrong.warning-diamond: The yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead, such as a sharp curve. A sign that tells you a law, such as a speed limit, is always a rectangle. The white rectangle is the one that means a law you must obey.
wrong.railroad-circle: The yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead. A sign that tells you a law, such as a speed limit, is always a rectangle. The white rectangle is the one that means a law you must obey.

steps.rule: A regulatory sign, which tells you about laws such as speed limits and lane use, is always a rectangle.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, a blue rectangle, and a red and white three-sided sign pointing down. Which sign means directions to towns and highways? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways, such as which exit to take and how far it is to a town. Green is the color for signs that guide you, and for the mileposts along the highway. The blue rectangle points to services for drivers, and the red and white three-sided sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first.

wrong.services-rect: The blue rectangle points to services for drivers, such as a rest area. The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways, because green is the color for signs that guide you.
wrong.yield-sign: The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first. The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways, because green is the color for signs that guide you.

steps.rule: Green is used for guide signs, which give directions, and for mileposts.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a white rectangle, an orange diamond, a yellow diamond, and a red eight-sided sign. Which sign means road work is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The orange diamond means road work is ahead, so you slow down and watch for workers and their machines. Orange is used for road work and for nothing else. The yellow diamond warns of other hazards, the white rectangle states a law, and the red eight-sided sign means stop.

wrong.law-rect: The white rectangle states a law you must obey, such as a speed limit. The orange diamond means road work is ahead, because orange is used for road work and for nothing else.
wrong.warning-diamond: The yellow diamond warns of other hazards ahead, such as a sharp curve, and road work has its own color. The orange diamond means road work is ahead, because orange is used for road work and for nothing else.
wrong.stop-sign: The red eight-sided sign means you must come to a complete stop. The orange diamond means road work is ahead, because orange is used for road work and for nothing else.

steps.rule: Orange is used only for construction and maintenance signs.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, an orange diamond, and a fluorescent yellow-green diamond. Which sign means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead, so you watch for children and people on foot. This bright color stands out in low light, fog and rain. The orange diamond means road work, and the green rectangle gives directions.

wrong.guide-rect: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways. The fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead, so you watch for children and people on foot.
wrong.roadwork-diamond: The orange diamond means road work is ahead, and orange is used for nothing else. The fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead, so you watch for children and people on foot.

steps.rule: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school zones and pedestrian areas such as crosswalks.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a fluorescent yellow-green diamond, an orange diamond, a red and white three-sided sign pointing down, and a blue rectangle. Which sign means a rest area or other services for drivers are ahead? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The blue rectangle means a rest area, police help or another service for drivers is ahead, because blue is the color for services for drivers. The orange diamond means road work, and the fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk. The red and white three-sided sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first.

wrong.school-diamond: The fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead. The blue rectangle means a rest area or another service for drivers is ahead, because blue is the color for services for drivers.
wrong.roadwork-diamond: The orange diamond means road work is ahead. The blue rectangle means a rest area or another service for drivers is ahead, because blue is the color for services for drivers.
wrong.yield-sign: The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first. The blue rectangle means a rest area or another service for drivers is ahead, because blue is the color for services for drivers.

steps.rule: Blue is used for motorist services, including police services and rest areas.

steps.prompt: A sign is yellow. What does its color tell you?
options: It warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.
It warns you that road work is ahead.
It gives you directions, such as which exit to take.
It tells you that a rest area is ahead.
steps.answer: It warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.

then.say: A yellow sign warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve, so you slow down and drive with care. Yellow is also used for school signs, and fluorescent yellow-green is now used for school zones too. Road work is orange, directions are green, and services such as rest areas are blue.

Road work signs are orange, and orange is used for nothing else. A yellow sign warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.
wrong.It gives you directions, such as which e: Directions are on green signs. A yellow sign warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.
Services for drivers, such as rest areas, are on blue signs. A yellow sign warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.

steps.rule: Yellow is the background for warning signs, except where orange is used, and for school signs.

steps.prompt: Every question in this lesson came down to one thing. What was it?
options: A sign's shape and color tell you what it means.
A sign's words tell you what it means.
A sign's place beside the road tells you what it means.
steps.answer: A sign's shape and color tell you what it means.

then.say: The shape and the color of a sign tell you its purpose, even from far away. That is how you know what a sign tells you to do before you can read it, and even when snow or dirt covers it.

The signs drawn in this lesson had no words on them, and their shape and color were enough to tell what each one meant. A sign's shape and color tell you what it means from far away, before you can read any words.
wrong.A sign's place beside the road tells you: Every sign drawn in this lesson stood beside the road, and each one meant something different. A sign's shape and color tell you what it means, even from far away.

steps.prompt: You are coming up to a steady yellow light. You can still stop safely before the intersection. You want to drive straight across. What do you do?
options: You slow down and stop before the intersection.
You speed up to get through before the light turns red.
You keep going at the same speed.
steps.answer: You slow down and stop before the intersection.

then.say: You slow down and stop before the intersection. A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red. If you were too close to stop safely, you would go on through the intersection, but you never speed up to get through before it turns red.

wrong.You speed up to get through before the l: A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red, and you never speed up to get through before it does. You can still stop safely, so you slow down and stop before the intersection.
You go on through a steady yellow light only when you are too close to stop safely, and here you can still stop. You slow down and stop before the intersection.

steps.rule: A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red, so you slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely.

steps.prompt: You have reached a flashing red light and want to drive straight across. No other car is in sight. What do you do?
options: You come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
You slow down and go through without stopping.
You stop and wait until the light turns green.
steps.answer: You come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
